- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; apply a “lag correction” — delay downward trend by 1–2 periods.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.5) within 5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; dampen forecast volatility by 20–40% in next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price deviates >3σ from 18-day moving average; adjust forecast toward historical mean if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with true trend.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.5), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use sentiment-weighted average of 3-day moving average and true price to anchor forecast.
